bootstrap.auto-fail-sins-evaluator:
- Re-implemented `src/services/network/{request,cache}.ts` or the routing/geocoding provider-fallback chains instead of reusing them
- Introduced a side effect, `fetch`, `Date.now()`-style ambient state, or storage access into `src/domain/**` (that layer stays pure)
- Reached `localStorage` directly from a component, hook, or feature instead of going through `src/services/storage/tripStorage.ts`
- Swallowed or masked a provider failure (routing, geocoding, weather, gas) so the UI shows a blank panel instead of an explicit error state
- Changed the persisted trip schema without a migration path for existing localStorage data
- Google OAuth client IDs, tokens, or any API key committed to code, logs, or fixtures
- Tests that assert nothing, or that mock the unit under test
- Live calls to OSRM, OpenRouteService, Photon, Nominatim, api.weather.gov, Open-Meteo, fueleconomy.gov, or Google APIs from tests
- {{EVALUATOR_AUTO_FAIL_TRIGGERS}}
bootstrap.auto-fail-sins-qa:
- Uncaught error or React warning in the browser console on an affected view
- A routing, geocoding, weather, or gas-price failure surfaced as a blank panel, a spinner that never resolves, or a raw error object
- An export (PDF, `.ics`, trip JSON) reported as generated but not actually produced, or produced empty/malformed
- Exported trip JSON that will not re-import into the app
- A Google OAuth token, refresh token, or API key visible in the DOM, console, network log, or an exported artifact
- A persisted trip made unreadable by the change, with no migration
- Success reported without the effect actually happening
- {{QA_AUTO_FAIL_TRIGGERS}}
bootstrap.auto-fail-triggers: `evaluator`: re-implemented `services/network` or the provider-fallback chains; side effects in `src/domain`; direct `localStorage` access outside `services/storage`; a swallowed provider failure; a persisted-schema change with no migration; secrets in code or fixtures; weak tests; live external calls from tests. `qa-evaluator`: console errors; a blank panel or raw error object where a provider failed; an export that is missing, empty, or won't re-import; a token or key visible in the DOM/console/network log; success reported without the effect.

bootstrap.execution-layers: The chain runs `src/types` + `src/config` (pure declarations, no imports from below) → `src/domain/{trip,weather,gas}` (pure rules and types, no side effects) → `src/services/*` (all side effects: `network/request.ts` + `network/cache.ts`, `maps/*` routing, `geocoding/*`, `weather/*`, `gas/*`, `storage/tripStorage.ts`, `drive/*`, `calendar/*`, `print/*`) → `src/hooks` → `src/features/{trip,map,weather}` + `src/components/common` → `src/app`. A layer may import only from layers to its left. `infra/` (Bicep, `azure.yaml`, `staticwebapp.config.json`), `scripts/`, and `.github/workflows/` sit outside the chain and are their own delivery lane.

bootstrap.mock-boundary: Mock at the service boundary, not at the transport primitive: stub the exported functions of `src/services/{maps,geocoding,weather,gas,drive,storage}/*` (or, for the service modules themselves, `src/services/network/request.ts`) — never patch global `fetch` ad hoc in a component test. Use Vitest's own tools: `vi.mock()` for module boundaries, `vi.fn()` / `vi.spyOn()` for functions, `vi.useFakeTimers()` for the date-driven trip and forecast logic, and `vi.stubGlobal('localStorage', ...)` when the node environment needs storage. Existing tests in `src/services/maps/googleMaps.test.ts` and `src/services/geocoding/autocompleteService.test.ts` are the reference shape. Note that `vitest.config.ts` sets `environment: 'node'` — a component test (`*.test.tsx`) that needs a DOM must declare `// @vitest-environment jsdom` at the top of the file.
bootstrap.models-map-caveats:
- **Copilot cost ceiling**: a subagent cannot run a *stronger* model than the session — the orchestrated session must run the `frontier` tier (`Claude Opus 5`); workers pin down. A too-strong pin makes the subagent not run at all, silently.
- **Copilot has no effort key**: drop `effort:` from every `.github/agents/*.agent.md`; tier alone carries the intent there.
- **Copilot model names are display names**, not slugs — `Claude Opus 5`, not `claude-opus-5`. The `model:` key also accepts an array (`['Claude Opus 5', 'GPT-6 Astra']`) which is how fallback is expressed in that harness.
- **Copilot nesting stays off** (kit default): `feature.agent.md` is the L1 orchestrator and spawns workers and evaluators directly; workers spawn nothing. `/setup` must not enable `chat.subagents.allowInvocationsFromSubagents`, and must not write `.vscode/settings.json` — this repo already has a `.vscode/` directory.
- **Claude Code env overrides**: `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` and `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` override frontmatter, and an org `availableModels` allowlist can cause pins to be ignored — an agent that self-reports a model other than the one requested is a signal, not a bug in the map.
- **Claude Code nesting depth**: this install merges `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=3` into `.claude/settings.json` so workers can spawn `terminal`. The default has flipped before — keep it pinned explicitly.
- **Claude Code aliases over dated IDs**: `opus`/`sonnet`/`haiku`/`fable` track the current generation; dated IDs rotate and go stale. Re-run `/setup` (or edit this file and re-emit) when a provider rotates names.
- Cursor and Codex are not targeted by this install; their caveats are omitted.
bootstrap.models-map-effort: Reasoning-effort pins: evaluators (`evaluator`, `qa-evaluator`, `diagnostician`) run `effort: high`, workers (`implementer`, `test-writer`, `terminal`) run `effort: medium` — set via Claude Code's `effort:` frontmatter key. GitHub Copilot has no effort key; drop the pin there and rely on tier alone. Cursor and Codex are not targeted by this install.

- **SPA UI** (`src/app`, `src/features/{trip,map,weather}`, `src/components/common`) — screenshots of the affected views from a running `npm run dev` server (trip form, TripTimeline, StopDrawer, MapLibre TripMap, WeatherPanel/StopWeatherForecast), plus a clean browser console and network log.

bootstrap.qa-surfaces-keep:
### SPA UI surfaces (`src/app`, `src/features/*`, `src/components/common`)
- Screenshots show the affected views rendering correctly at both a desktop and a narrow viewport.
- Browser console is free of errors and React warnings; network log shows no failed requests.
- Loading, empty, and error states are each explicitly rendered — never a blank panel.
- Keyboard reachability and labeling hold for any form control or button touched.

### External API integration surfaces (`src/services/{maps,geocoding,weather,gas}`)
- The exact request issued is shown, together with the response shape the code handles.
- Failure and fallback paths are exercised, not just the happy path: OSRM → alternate OSRM → OpenRouteService for routing, and the geocoding/weather providers' error responses.
- Rate-limit, timeout, and malformed-response handling produce a user-visible message rather than a thrown error.
- No live network call originates from a test; evidence from tests is the mocked fixture output.

### Export artifact surfaces (PDF, iCal, trip JSON)
- The generated file is produced and inspected, not merely reported as generated.
- PDF output contains the stops, dates, and map capture for the trip under test.
- `.ics` output parses and carries one event per dated stop with correct arrival/departure.
- Exported trip JSON re-imports cleanly into the app with no data loss.

### Cross-cutting
- No Google OAuth token, refresh token, or API key appears in the DOM, console, network log, or any exported artifact.
- No change silently breaks the persisted localStorage trip schema without a migration.
bootstrap.quality-check-commands: Cycle-end quality gate for this project — all four run from the repo root; there is one npm workspace and no `cd` requirement.
bootstrap.shared-libs:
a shared HTTP + caching layer (`src/services/network/request.ts`, `src/services/network/cache.ts`), a single persistence entry point (`src/services/storage/tripStorage.ts`), provider-fallback chains for routing (`src/services/maps/openSourceRouting.ts`, `routesService.ts`) and geocoding (`src/services/geocoding/{geocodingService,autocompleteService}.ts`), the Google Drive auth/sync stack (`src/services/drive/*`), pure domain rules under `src/domain/{trip,weather,gas}`, env access via `src/config/env.ts`, and reusable UI in `src/components/common` — build on them.
  Never re-implement what these provide: no bare `fetch` in a feature or hook, no direct `localStorage` access outside `tripStorage.ts`, no `import.meta.env` outside `src/config/env.ts`, and no second routing or geocoding client.

tokens.STACK_SUMMARY: React 19 + Vite 7 + TypeScript 5.9 client-only SPA (npm, ESM, no backend), deployed to Azure Static Web Apps via azd/Bicep in infra/. Code lanes run types/config -> domain (pure rules for trip, weather, gas) -> services (network, storage, Google Drive sync, PDF/iCal export) -> hooks -> features (trip, map, weather) + components/common -> app. All persistence is browser localStorage; all mapping, routing, geocoding and weather come from free keyless public APIs (OpenStreetMap/MapLibre, OSRM/OpenRouteService, Photon/Nominatim, NOAA + Open-Meteo). Tests are Vitest 2.1 (node environment); lint is ESLint 9 flat config; type-checking is tsc -b.
